input.plan:
# Phase 1: PLM project structure

Work from the latest `origin/main` (it already has [PLM_SPEC.md](PLM_SPEC.md), which the local snapshot is missing). Create branch `cursor/plm-project-structure-48f7`. This PR is **structure + runnable skeleton only** — not entity/metadata/workflow implementation.

Spec source of truth: [PLM_SPEC.md](PLM_SPEC.md) sections 5–6, 36–40 (Phase 1).

## Scope

In:

- Full monorepo tree from spec §6
- Maven aggregator for Java (Quarkus default; kernel/modules as empty JARs with explicit boundaries)
- pnpm workspace for Next.js + TS packages
- Docker Compose for local appliance (`make dev`)
- Root `Makefile`, `README.md`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`
- Minimal Quarkus health + Next.js shell
- Flyway placeholder + GitHub Actions CI that compiles

Out:

- Entity kernel, Cerbos policies beyond a stub, Authelia login flow wiring, AI/MCP, domain modules, shadcn screens

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph apps [apps]
    web[Next.js web]
    api[Quarkus API]
  end
  subgraph kernel [kernel JARs]
    entity[entity]
    metadata[metadata]
    other[other kernel modules]
  end
  subgraph infra [compose]
    pg[PostgreSQL]
    rustfs[RustFS]
    redis[Valkey]
    authelia[Authelia]
    cerbos[Cerbos]
  end
  web -->|REST| api
  api --> kernel
  api --> pg
  api --> rustfs
  api --> redis
  api --> cerbos
  web --> authelia
```

## Layout to create

Match spec §6 at repo root (do not nest under an extra `plm/` folder). Keep existing `LICENSE` and `PLM_SPEC.md`. README will point at `PLM_SPEC.md` rather than duplicating a `SPEC.md`.

- **Apps:** [`apps/api/quarkus`](apps/api/quarkus) (Quarkus REST, Flyway, health/liveness/readiness), [`apps/web/nextjs`](apps/web/nextjs) (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, Geist)
- **Kernel:** one Maven module per spec module under [`kernel/`](kernel/) (`entity`, `metadata`, `relationship`, `search`, `semantic`, `ontology`, `graph`, `workflow`, `audit`, `document`, `authorization`, `ai`, `extension`) — each with `src/main/java/io/agentplm/kernel/<name>/package-info.java` and a one-line README
- **Domain modules:** empty Maven modules under [`modules/`](modules/) (`product`, `material`, `supplier`, `season`, `collection`, `sample`, `bom`, `specification`)
- **Extensions:** placeholder dirs + manifests under [`extensions/`](extensions/) (`apparel`, `footwear`, `cpg`, `sustainability`)
- **SDKs:** [`sdk/java`](sdk/java) (Maven), [`sdk/typescript`](sdk/typescript) (package.json stub)
- **Packages:** [`packages/core-schema`](packages/core-schema), [`packages/semantic-model`](packages/semantic-model), [`packages/ui-extension-sdk`](packages/ui-extension-sdk)
- **Schemas / policies / infra / migrations:** [`schemas/core`](schemas/core), [`schemas/extensions`](schemas/extensions), [`policies/cerbos`](policies/cerbos), [`infra/{postgres,rustfs,authelia,cerbos,redis,nginx}`](infra/), [`migrations/`](migrations/)

## Java / Maven

- Root [`pom.xml`](pom.xml): `groupId` `io.agentplm`, Java 25, Quarkus BOM, aggregator listing kernel + modules + `sdk/java` + `apps/api/quarkus`
- Quarkus app depends on kernel modules (empty JARs) so module boundaries are real from day one
- `quarkus-rest`, `quarkus-hibernate-orm-panache` (unused until Phase 2), `quarkus-jdbc-postgresql`, `quarkus-flyway`, `quarkus-hibernate-validator`, `quarkus-opentelemetry`, `quarkus-smallrye-health`, `quarkus-config-yaml`
- Flyway location: repo-root [`migrations/`](migrations/) copied into the API image; first script `V1__extensions.sql` enables `vector` / `pg_trgm` only (no entity tables yet)
- Package convention: `io.agentplm.kernel.*`, `io.agentplm.modules.*`, `io.agentplm.api`

## Frontend / pnpm

- [`pnpm-workspace.yaml`](pnpm-workspace.yaml) for `apps/web/nextjs`, `sdk/typescript`, `packages/*`
- Minimal Next.js app: health/status page, Tailwind, Geist, env `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`
- No shadcn install sweep yet (Phase 10); add Tailwind so later UI work has a base

## Docker Compose + Makefile

Files: [`docker-compose.yml`](docker-compose.yml) (shared services), [`docker-compose.dev.yml`](docker-compose.dev.yml) (dev overrides, bind mounts where useful), [`docker-compose.prod.yml`](docker-compose.prod.yml) (nginx + no bind mounts).

`make dev` → `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build`

Services from spec §36:

| Service | Image approach |
|---|---|
| postgres | `pgvector/pgvector` on newest available Postgres (prefer 17/18 if 19 images are not published yet); init from `infra/postgres` |
| rustfs | official RustFS S3-compatible image + named volume |
| redis | Valkey |
| authelia | config stub in `infra/authelia` (login wiring later) |
| cerbos | `infra/cerbos` + empty `policies/cerbos` allow-all stub for health |
| api | Dockerfile in `apps/api/quarkus` |
| web | Dockerfile in `apps/web/nextjs` |
| nginx | prod compose only |

[`.env.example`](.env.example): DB, S3, Redis, OIDC, Cerbos, API/web URLs. No secrets committed.

## Makefile / CI / docs

- Targets: `dev`, `down`, `api`, `web`, `test`, `migrate` (stubs where not yet implemented)
- [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml): Maven `verify`, pnpm `lint`/`build`, `docker compose config`
- [`README.md`](README.md): product one-liner, how to run `make dev`, stack table, pointer to `PLM_SPEC.md`, current phase

## Verification (after implementation)

- `./mvnw -q verify` succeeds
- `pnpm --filter web build` (or equivalent) succeeds
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml config` is valid
- API `/q/health` and web homepage respond when compose is up (or document if a service image is unavailable in this environment)

## Later phases (not this PR)

Phase 2+ from spec §40: entity kernel, metadata, relationships, core PLM, search, semantic, workflow, AI/MCP, UI, extensions.

    ("sample", "Samples and development requests."),
    ("bom", "Bills of materials and BOM lines."),
    ("specification", "Product and material specifications and measurements."),
]

def write(path: Path, content: str):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(content.lstrip("\n") if content.startswith("\n") else content)
    if not content.endswith("\n"):
        path.write_text(path.read_text() + "\n")

def maven_module_pom(parent_artifact, artifact, name, relative_parent, description):
    return f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>io.agentplm</groupId>
    <artifactId>{parent_artifact}</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <relativePath>{relative_parent}</relativePath>
  </parent>

  <artifactId>{artifact}</artifactId>
  <name>{name}</name>
  <description>{description}</description>
</project>
'''

def package_info(package, summary):
    return f'''/**
 * {summary}
 */
package {package};
'''

def readme(title, body):
    return f"# {title}\n\n{body}\n"

# --- kernel aggregator ---
kernel_modules_xml = "\n".join(f"    <module>{n}</module>" for n, _ in KERNEL)
write(ROOT / "kernel/pom.xml", f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>io.agentplm</groupId>
    <artifactId>agent-plm</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <relativePath>../pom.xml</relativePath>
  </parent>

  <artifactId>plm-kernel</artifactId>
  <packaging>pom</packaging>
  <name>PLM Kernel</name>
  <description>Logical kernel modules for the AI-native PLM platform.</description>

  <modules>
{kernel_modules_xml}
  </modules>
</project>
''')

write(ROOT / "kernel/README.md", readme("PLM Kernel",
    "Logical modules of the PLM kernel. These are Maven JARs inside a modular monolith, not separate services."))

for name, desc in KERNEL:
    write(ROOT / f"kernel/{name}/pom.xml", maven_module_pom(
        "plm-kernel", f"plm-kernel-{name}", f"PLM Kernel — {name}", "../pom.xml", desc))
    write(ROOT / f"kernel/{name}/README.md", readme(f"kernel/{name}", desc))
    pkg = name.replace("-", "")
    write(ROOT / f"kernel/{name}/src/main/java/io/agentplm/kernel/{pkg}/package-info.java",
          package_info(f"io.agentplm.kernel.{pkg}", desc))
    write(ROOT / f"kernel/{name}/src/test/java/.gitkeep", "")

# --- domain aggregator ---
module_xml = "\n".join(f"    <module>{n}</module>" for n, _ in MODULES)
write(ROOT / "modules/pom.xml", f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>io.agentplm</groupId>
    <artifactId>agent-plm</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <relativePath>../pom.xml</relativePath>
  </parent>

  <artifactId>plm-modules</artifactId>
  <packaging>pom</packaging>
  <name>PLM Domain Modules</name>
  <description>Opinionated core PLM domain modules built on the kernel.</description>

  <modules>
{module_xml}
  </modules>
</project>
''')

write(ROOT / "modules/README.md", readme("PLM Domain Modules",
    "Core PLM domain concepts. All modules use the same Entity/Metadata/Relationship kernel."))

for name, desc in MODULES:
    write(ROOT / f"modules/{name}/pom.xml", maven_module_pom(
        "plm-modules", f"plm-module-{name}", f"PLM Module — {name}", "../pom.xml", desc))
    write(ROOT / f"modules/{name}/README.md", readme(f"modules/{name}", desc))
    write(ROOT / f"modules/{name}/src/main/java/io/agentplm/modules/{name}/package-info.java",
          package_info(f"io.agentplm.modules.{name}", desc))
    write(ROOT / f"modules/{name}/src/test/java/.gitkeep", "")

# Agent PLM

Open-source, AI-native Product Lifecycle Management. Opinionated PLM product plus an extensible kernel.

Specification: [PLM_SPEC.md](PLM_SPEC.md)

**Current phase:** 1 — platform skeleton (monorepo, Compose, health checks). Domain kernel is not implemented yet.

## Stack

| Layer | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| API | Java 25, Quarkus 3.39 |
| UI | Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
| Data | PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector (JSON, FTS, graph later) |
| Objects | RustFS (S3) |
| Cache | Valkey |
| AuthN | Authelia |
| AuthZ | Cerbos |
| Dev appliance | Docker Compose |

## Repository

```
apps/api/quarkus     Quarkus modular monolith
apps/web/nextjs      Next.js UI
kernel/              Logical kernel JARs
modules/             Core PLM domain modules
extensions/          Industry packages
sdk/                 Java and TypeScript SDKs
packages/            Shared TS schema/UI packages
schemas/             Declarative schema YAML
policies/cerbos      Authorization policies
infra/               Compose service config
migrations/          Flyway SQL
```

## Prerequisites

- JDK 25
- Node.js 22 and pnpm 10
- Docker Compose (for `make dev`)

Copy environment defaults:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

## Commands

```bash
make dev              # start the full local stack
make down             # stop Compose
make test             # Maven verify + Next.js lint/build
make compose-config   # validate Compose files
./mvnw verify         # backend only
pnpm --filter @agent-plm/web dev
```

API health: `http://localhost:8080/q/health` and `http://localhost:8080/api/health`  
UI: `http://localhost:3000`

## Notes

- Redis/Valkey is not the system of record.
- Authelia and Cerbos are started in Compose; login and real policies come in later phases.
- PostgreSQL 19 from the spec is not used yet; Compose uses a pgvector image on Postgres 17 until 19 is published.

Authelia 4 was failing for three separate reasons. All three are addressed.

**1. Read-only mounts** — Config files were mounted with `:ro`, but the Authelia entrypoint runs `chown` on `/config`.  
**Fix:** Mount the whole `./infra/authelia` directory read-write. Runtime state goes under `runtime/` (SQLite, notifications).

**2. Invalid cookie domain** — `localhost` is not allowed; Authelia requires a dotted domain or an IP.  
**Fix:** Use `127.0.0.1` for session cookies and access-control rules.

**3. HTTP session URLs** — Authelia 4 requires HTTPS for `authelia_url` and `default_redirection_url`.  
**Fix:** Enable TLS in Authelia and use `https://127.0.0.1:9091`. Dev certs are generated by `make authelia-certs` (also runs before `make dev`).

**Restart:**

```bash
make authelia-certs
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up authelia -d --force-recreate
```

Or restart the full stack with `make dev`.

Authelia portal: **https://127.0.0.1:9091/** (accept the self-signed cert in your browser). The Next.js app is still on plain HTTP at `http://localhost:3000` until login is wired in a later phase.

Yes — there’s a lot of room to speed it up. The current Dockerfile already does dependency-layer caching, but most of the cost is elsewhere.

## What’s slow today

1. **Huge build context** — Compose builds from the repo root (`.`), but [`.dockerignore`](.dockerignore) only excludes `node_modules`, `target`, etc. It still sends `kernel/`, `modules/`, `apps/api/`, `infra/`, `migrations/`, and more on every build.
2. **Full workspace install** — `pnpm install` pulls all 6 workspace packages, even though the web app only needs a subset.
3. **Next.js build does extra work** — `next build` runs ESLint and type-checking inside the image (you already lint in CI).
4. **No BuildKit cache mounts** — when a layer invalidates, `pnpm install` and `.next/cache` start from scratch.
5. **`make dev` rebuilds the image** — for local dev, a bind-mounted `pnpm dev` is usually much faster than rebuilding Docker layers.

## Highest-impact fixes

| Change | Expected gain |
|--------|----------------|
| Expand `.dockerignore` for web builds (`kernel/`, `modules/`, `apps/api/`, `infra/`, `migrations/`, …) | Faster context upload + fewer cache busts |
| BuildKit cache mounts for pnpm store + `.next/cache` | Much faster rebuilds after source changes |
| `pnpm install --filter @agent-plm/web...` | Smaller install |
| `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds: true` in Docker (keep lint in CI) | Shorter `next build` |
| Dev compose override: mount source + `pnpm dev`, skip image build | Fastest local iteration |

```dockerfile
WORKDIR /repo

COPY package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-lock.yaml .npmrc ./
COPY apps/web/nextjs/package.json apps/web/nextjs/
COPY sdk/typescript/package.json sdk/typescript/
COPY packages/*/package.json packages/
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=pnpm-store,target=/pnpm/store \

FROM deps AS build
COPY apps/web/nextjs apps/web/nextjs
COPY sdk/typescript sdk/typescript
COPY packages packages
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
RUN --mount=type=cache,id=next-cache,target=/repo/apps/web/nextjs/.next/cache \
    pnpm --filter @agent-plm/web build
```


# Create PLM Entity

Implement a new core PLM entity by copying the **Season** reference implementation. Every entity shares the `entity` + `entity_type` kernel and adds a type-specific extension table.

## Before You Start

Gather (or infer from PLM_SPEC.md):

| Input | Example (Season) |
|-------|------------------|
| Entity name (PascalCase) | `Season` |
| Plural REST path | `/api/seasons` |
| UI route prefix | `/seasons` |
| Status enum values | `DRAFT`, `ACTIVE`, `CLOSED` |
| Type-specific fields | `code`, `calendarYear`, `startsOn`, `endsOn` |
| Unique business key | `code` |
| Archive semantics | DELETE sets status to terminal enum (Season → `CLOSED`) |

Read the Season reference files listed in [examples.md](examples.md) before writing code.

## Workflow Checklist

Copy and track progress:

```
- [ ] 1. Plan schema + allocate entity_type UUID
- [ ] 2. Flyway migration (both locations)
- [ ] 3. Domain module (modules/{entity})
- [ ] 4. EntityTypes constant (kernel/entity)
- [ ] 5. API persistence + service + resource
- [ ] 6. Wire Maven dependencies
- [ ] 7. Next.js lib + components + pages + nav
- [ ] 8. Verify (build, API smoke test, UI)
```

---

## Step 1 — Plan Schema

**Naming conventions** (see [reference.md](reference.md)):

- SQL table: `{entity_snake}` (e.g. `season`)
- Java record: `{Entity}Record` in `api.persistence`
- Module package: `io.agentplm.modules.{entity}`
- REST package: `io.agentplm.api.{entity}`

**Entity type UUID**: add a constant to `EntityTypes.java`. Use the next sequential placeholder UUID (Season = `11111111-…`, Product = `22222222-…`, Material = `33333333-…`, etc.) unless the spec defines one.

**Migration version**: next `V{N}__{description}.sql` in both:

- `migrations/`
- `apps/api/quarkus/src/main/resources/db/migration/`

Migration must:

1. `INSERT INTO entity_type` for the new type (skip if reusing V2 tables).
2. `CREATE TABLE {entity}` with `id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES entity (id) ON DELETE CASCADE`.
3. Add unique constraints and CHECK constraints for domain invariants.
4. Keep `entity` and `audit_event` unchanged (created in V2).

---

## Step 2 — Domain Module

Location: `modules/{entity}/`

Create (mirror Season):

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `{Entity}Status.java` | Enum for lifecycle states |
| `{Entity}Draft.java` | Immutable record of all editable fields |
| `{Entity}ValidationException.java` | Domain validation error |
| `{Entity}Rules.java` | `normalize()` + `validate()` |
| `{Entity}RulesTest.java` | Unit tests for rules |

Rules class responsibilities:

- Trim strings; uppercase codes if applicable.
- Default status to first draft state when null.
- Throw `{Entity}ValidationException` with clear messages.
- Keep validation **pure** — no DB or HTTP.

Add module to `modules/pom.xml` if not already listed. Artifact: `plm-module-{entity}`.

---

## Step 3 — API Layer

Location: `apps/api/quarkus/src/main/java/io/agentplm/api/`

### Persistence (`api.persistence`)

- `{Entity}Record.java` — JPA entity mapped to extension table.
- `{Entity}RecordRepository.java` — Panache repo with `findBy{UniqueKey}()` and `listAllOrdered()`.

Reuse existing: `PlmEntity`, `PlmEntityRepository`, `AuditEvent`, `AuditEventRepository`.

### REST (`api.{entity}`)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `{Entity}Request.java` | Input DTO with `@NotBlank` on required fields, optional `version` for optimistic locking |
| `{Entity}Response.java` | Output DTO including `id`, `version`, timestamps |
| `{Entity}Service.java` | CRUD + audit |
| `{Entity}Resource.java` | JAX-RS at `/api/{entities}` |

**Service pattern** (follow `SeasonService` exactly):

1. `list()` — join extension table with `PlmEntity`, map to response.
2. `get(id)` — load both rows or throw `NotFoundException`.
3. `create(request)` — normalize → validate → check unique key → persist `PlmEntity` (with `EntityTypes.{ENTITY}`) + extension row → audit `CREATE`.
4. `update(id, request)` — optimistic lock via `version` → unique key check excluding self → update both rows → audit `UPDATE`.
5. `archive(id)` — set terminal status on `PlmEntity` → audit `ARCHIVE`. Do **not** delete rows.

```xml
<dependency>

  <version>${project.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

---

## Step 4 — Next.js UI

Location: `apps/web/nextjs/src/`

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `lib/{entities}.ts` | Types, `SeasonInput`-like input type, CRUD fetch helpers |
| `components/{Entity}Form.tsx` | Create/edit form (client component) |
| `components/{Entity}List.tsx` | List with links to detail |
| `app/{entities}/page.tsx` | List page |

**API client**: copy `lib/seasons.ts` pattern. Use `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (default `http://localhost:8080`). Parse `{ error: string }` from failed responses.

**UI conventions**:

- Wrap pages in `AppShell`.
- List page: heading, description, "New {entity}" link, `{Entity}List`.
- Form: `name`, `code` (if applicable), `description`, `status` select, type-specific fields.
- Pass `version` from `initial` on update for optimistic locking.
- Add nav link in `AppShell.tsx`.

Match existing styling: dark theme, `border-white/15`, `var(--accent)`, `var(--muted)`.

Run in order:

```bash

./mvnw -pl modules/{entity} test

# API compile + tests

# Frontend typecheck
cd apps/web/nextjs && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
```

Implemented Hibernate 7.4 `@Temporal`, `@Audited`, and UUID v7 on a shared base class. Summary:

## Architecture

**`PlmEntity`** is now a `@MappedSuperclass` — the base for all JPA entities:

```1:27:apps/api/quarkus/src/main/java/io/agentplm/api/persistence/PlmEntity.java
@MappedSuperclass
@Temporal
@Audited
public abstract class PlmEntity {

    @Id
    @UuidGenerator(style = UuidGenerator.Style.VERSION_7)
    public UUID id;
}
```

**Concrete entities extend it** and declare their history/audit tables:

| Class | Table | History | Audit log |
|-------|-------|---------|-----------|
| `EntityRecord` | `entity` | `entity_history` | `entity_aud` |
| `SeasonRecord` | `season` | `season_history` | `season_aud` |
| `AuditEvent` | `audit_event` | `audit_event_history` | `audit_event_aud` |

The kernel row type moved from `PlmEntity` → **`EntityRecord`** (maps to the `entity` table). `PlmEntityRepository` now uses `EntityRecord`.

## Configuration

`application.yml` enables Hibernate temporal history tables and the changelog-backed changeset supplier:

- `hibernate.temporal.table_strategy`: `HISTORY_TABLE`
- `hibernate.temporal.changeset_id_supplier`: `PlmChangesetSupplier`

Supporting types: `PlmChangeset` (`@Changelog`) and `PlmChangesetSupplier`.

## Migration & Postgres

- **`V3__temporal_and_audit_tables.sql`** — creates `plm_changeset`, `*_history`, and `*_aud` tables (in both `migrations/` and quarkus resources).
- **Docker Compose** bumped to `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` for PostgreSQL 18 native UUID v7 support (IDs are still generated in Hibernate via `@UuidGenerator`).

## Service changes

`SeasonService` no longer calls `UUID.randomUUID()`. It persists `EntityRecord` first; Hibernate assigns a time-ordered UUID v7, then reuses `entity.id` for `SeasonRecord`.

## Two audit layers (intentional)

1. **Hibernate `@Audited`** — ORM change log in `*_aud` tables (Envers-compatible `rev` / `revtype` columns).
2. **Application `AuditEvent`** — business audit trail (CREATE/UPDATE/ARCHIVE) you already had; unchanged in purpose, now also `@Temporal` / `@Audited`.

After pulling, run `make dev` (or reset DB if V3 hasn’t applied yet). Existing UUID v4 rows remain valid; new rows get UUID v7.

Add a job that runs **only after all checks pass**, **only on `main`**:

```yaml
publish-wiki:
  name: Publish GitHub Wiki
  needs: [backend, frontend, compose]
  if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  permissions:
    contents: write   # required to push to *.wiki.git
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Build wiki content
      run: ./scripts/build-wiki.sh   # see below

    - name: Publish to GitHub Wiki
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      run: |
        git clone "REDACTED" wiki
        rsync -av --delete wiki-out/ wiki/
        cd wiki
        git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
        git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
        git add -A
        git diff --staged --quiet || git commit -m "Sync wiki from ${GITHUB_SHA:0:7}"
        git push
```

Why this shape:

- `needs:` ensures publish runs **after** backend/frontend/compose succeed.
- `if:` limits it to **main pushes** (not PRs).
- `rsync --delete` keeps wiki in sync when you remove pages.

If `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot push to the wiki (some org policies block it), create a PAT with **repo** scope and store it as `WIKI_PAT`, then use that instead.

---

## What to publish (content strategy)

Don’t dump the whole repo into the wiki. Curate a **`docs/wiki/`** (or generated `wiki-out/`) tree that explains how Agent PLM works.

Suggested pages from what you already have:

| Wiki page | Source |
|-----------|--------|
| `Home.md` | `README.md` (overview, stack, commands) |
| `Product-Spec.md` | `PLM_SPEC.md` (or split into chapters) |
| `Architecture.md` | PLM_SPEC sections 2–4 (kernel, entity model) |
| `Local-Development.md` | README + `infra/README.md` |
| `Entity-Kernel.md` | `.cursor/skills/create-plm-entity/` + Seasons example |
| `API-Conventions.md` | `.cursor/rules/api/quarkus.mdc` |
| `Modules.md` | `modules/README.md` + links to season/product stubs |
| `Roadmap.md` | `todo.md` (if you want it public) |

A small build script (`scripts/build-wiki.sh`) can:

1. Copy/transform selected markdown into `wiki-out/`.
2. Rewrite relative links (`PLM_SPEC.md` → `Product-Spec`).
3. Add a `Home.md` sidebar-style index linking all pages.
4. Optionally strip internal-only content (`.cursor/`, agent notes).

Example skeleton:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
OUT=wiki-out
rm -rf "$OUT" && mkdir -p "$OUT"

cp README.md "$OUT/Home.md"
cp PLM_SPEC.md "$OUT/Product-Spec.md"
cp infra/README.md "$OUT/Infrastructure.md"
# ... more copies / pandoc / sed for link fixes
```

---

## Alternative: dedicated workflow file

Many teams use a separate workflow so wiki publish is independent of PR CI:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish-wiki.yml
name: Publish Wiki
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'README.md'
      - 'PLM_SPEC.md'
      - 'docs/wiki/**'
      - 'scripts/build-wiki.sh'
  workflow_dispatch:   # manual “Publish now” button
```

You can still gate it on CI success with **branch protection + required checks**, or trigger it from the main CI workflow using `workflow_run`:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
# then if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
```

That gives you “publish only when CI is green” without cramming everything into one file.

---

## Wiki-specific gotchas

1. **Link format** — Wiki uses `[[Page-Name]]` or relative links between `.md` files; GitHub-style `](PLM_SPEC.md)` links from the main repo will break unless rewritten.
2. **Size limits** — `PLM_SPEC.md` is ~1800 lines; consider splitting into multiple wiki pages for readability.
3. **No PR preview** — Wiki updates go live on push; use a `docs/wiki/` folder in the main repo as the source of truth and review changes via normal PRs.
4. **Images** — Put images in the wiki repo or use absolute URLs; relative image paths from the main repo won’t work unless copied.
5. **Duplicate audit systems** — Your app has both Hibernate `@Audited` and application `AuditEvent`; document that clearly so wiki readers aren’t confused.

---

## GitHub Pages vs Wiki

| | Wiki | GitHub Pages |
|--|------|--------------|
| Setup | Clone + push markdown | `docs/` + Pages action |
| Search/navigation | Basic | Better with MkDocs/Docusaurus |
| Versioning | Single live version | Can version docs |
| CI pattern | Push to `*.wiki.git` | Deploy static site |

You asked specifically for the wiki URL — the git-push approach above is the standard way.

1. Enable wiki on `agent-plm/agent-plm`.
2. Add `docs/wiki/` (or `scripts/build-wiki.sh`) as the curated source.
3. Manually clone the wiki once, push an initial `Home.md`, confirm permissions.
4. Add `publish-wiki` job with `needs: [backend, frontend, compose]`.
5. Iterate on page structure (start with Home + Product Spec + Local Development).

# How Agent PLM Works

Agent PLM is an open-source, AI-native Product Lifecycle Management platform built as a **monorepo + Docker Compose appliance**.

## Product shape

- **Opinionated PLM product** — core concepts (Product, Season, Material, Supplier, BOM, etc.) work out of the box.
- **Extensible kernel** — entity identity, metadata, relationships, search, workflow, and authorization are shared across all types.
- **Same patterns everywhere** — every core type uses the universal entity kernel plus a type-specific extension table.

## Runtime stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| API | Java 25, Quarkus 3.39, Hibernate ORM 7.4 |
| UI | Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
| Database | PostgreSQL + pgvector (Flyway migrations) |
| Objects | RustFS (S3-compatible) |
| Cache | Valkey |
| AuthN | Authelia (local dev) |
| AuthZ | Cerbos (policies in `policies/cerbos`) |

## Request flow (Seasons example)

1. Browser calls Next.js at `/seasons`.
2. UI fetches JSON from Quarkus at `/api/seasons`.
3. `SeasonService` validates input via `SeasonRules` in `modules/season`.
4. Service persists `EntityRecord` (kernel row) + `SeasonRecord` (extension row) with the same UUID.
5. Application `AuditEvent` rows record CREATE / UPDATE / ARCHIVE for the API operation.
6. Hibernate `@Temporal` / `@Audited` maintain history and change logs in companion tables.

## Repository layout

See [[Home]] for the directory map. Deep specification lives in [[Product-Spec]].

## Current phase

Phase 2 — **Seasons** is the first end-to-end feature (Flyway schema, domain module, REST API, Next.js UI).

Future phases add Product, Material, Supplier, auth integration, and semantic/AI capabilities per the product spec.

# Entity Kernel

Every core PLM type shares the same identity and lifecycle columns in the `entity` table, with type-specific fields in an extension table.

## Two-table pattern

| Table | JPA type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `EntityRecord` | Name, status, JSON attributes, audit columns, optimistic lock |
| `{type}` | `{Type}Record` | Business fields (e.g. season `code`, dates) |

Both rows share the same primary key (`id`). The extension table references `entity(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`.

## Base class: `PlmEntity`

All JPA persistence types extend `PlmEntity` (`@MappedSuperclass`):

- **UUID v7** — `@UuidGenerator(style = VERSION_7)` for time-ordered IDs
- **@Temporal** — row history in `{table}_history` (Hibernate 7.4)
- **@Audited** — change log in `{table}_aud` with changeset ids

Concrete entities declare `@Temporal.HistoryTable` and `@Audited.Table` names matching Flyway (`V3__temporal_and_audit_tables.sql`).

## Creating a new entity type

1. Flyway migration — `entity_type` row + extension table
2. Domain module — `{Entity}Draft`, `{Entity}Rules`, tests in `modules/{entity}`
3. API — `EntityRecord` + `{Entity}Record`, service, REST resource
4. UI — Next.js lib, form, list, pages

Season is the reference implementation. See [[How-It-Works]] and the in-repo **create-plm-entity** Cursor skill.

## Entity type IDs

Fixed UUIDs in `kernel/entity/EntityTypes.java` (e.g. `SEASON = 11111111-…`). Migrations must use the same UUID in `INSERT INTO entity_type`.

# Local Development

## Prerequisites

- JDK 25
- Node.js 22 and pnpm 10
- Docker Compose

```bash
cp .env.example .env
make authelia-certs   # once, for HTTPS Authelia on plm.lvh.me
make dev              # full stack
```

## Endpoints

| Service | URL |
| --- | --- |
| UI | http://localhost:3000 |
| Seasons UI | http://localhost:3000/seasons |
| API health | http://localhost:8080/api/health |
| Seasons API | http://localhost:8080/api/seasons |
| Authelia | https://plm.lvh.me:9091 (HTTPS only) |

## Common commands

```bash
make down             # stop Compose
make test             # Maven verify + Next.js lint/build
./mvnw verify         # backend only
pnpm --filter @agent-plm/web dev   # UI outside Docker (optional)
```

## Infrastructure

Compose services: PostgreSQL (pgvector), RustFS, Valkey, Authelia, Cerbos, Quarkus API, Next.js web. Configuration lives under `infra/`. See [[Infrastructure]].

## Notes

- Valkey is not the system of record.
- Authelia and Cerbos start in Compose; full login flows arrive in later phases.
- Web dev uses `Dockerfile.dev` with bind mounts; production uses `apps/web/nextjs/Dockerfile`.

name: Publish Wiki

on:
  # Publish after main-branch CI succeeds (independent workflow file from ci.yml).
  # Note: workflow_run inherits a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN from CI — set secret WIKI_PAT.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  # Doc-only changes on main can publish without waiting for a separate CI trigger.
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "README.md"
      - "PLM_SPEC.md"
      - "docs/wiki/**"
      - "scripts/build-wiki.sh"
      - "infra/README.md"
      - "modules/README.md"
      - "kernel/README.md"
      - "migrations/README.md"
      - ".github/workflows/publish-wiki.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: publish-wiki
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  publish:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      github.event_name == 'push' ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Resolve source ref
        id: ref
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_run" ]; then
            echo "sha=${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "sha=${{ github.sha }}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          fi

      - name: Check wiki credentials
        env:
          WIKI_PAT: ${{ secrets.WIKI_PAT }}
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_run" ] && [ -z "${WIKI_PAT}" ]; then
            echo "::error::Publish Wiki was triggered by CI (workflow_run). GitHub does not grant write access to GITHUB_TOKEN in that case. Add repository secret WIKI_PAT (classic PAT with repo scope), or run this workflow manually via workflow_dispatch after merging to main."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "${WIKI_PAT}" ]; then
            echo "WIKI_PAT not set; using GITHUB_TOKEN (requires repo Settings → Actions → General → Read and write permissions)."
          else
            echo "Using WIKI_PAT for wiki git access."
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ steps.ref.outputs.sha }}

      - name: Build wiki pages
        run: bash scripts/build-wiki.sh wiki-out

      - name: Publish to GitHub Wiki
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WIKI_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          WIKI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WIKI_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          WIKI_URL="REDACTED github.repository }}.wiki.git"

          echo "Checking wiki API access..."
          gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}" --jq '{has_wiki: .has_wiki, permissions: .permissions}' || true
          PAGE_COUNT="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/wiki/pages" --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "unavailable")"
          echo "Existing wiki pages: ${PAGE_COUNT}"

          clone_wiki() {
            git clone "${WIKI_URL}" wiki-repo
          }

          if ! clone_wiki 2>/tmp/wiki-clone.err; then
            echo "Wiki git clone failed (often means no pages yet or token lacks access):"
            cat /tmp/wiki-clone.err
            echo "Bootstrapping wiki via GitHub API..."
            if ! gh api --method POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/wiki/pages" \
              -f title='Home' \
              -f body='Initializing Agent PLM wiki from CI.' \
              -f format='markdown'; then
              echo "::error::Could not create the first wiki page. Confirm Wiki is enabled, then add repository secret WIKI_PAT (classic PAT with repo scope) and re-run. Org repos may also need Settings → Actions → General → Read and write permissions."
              exit 1
            fi
            clone_wiki
          fi

          rsync -av --delete wiki-out/ wiki-repo/
          cd wiki-repo
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A
          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "Wiki already up to date."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "Sync wiki from agent-plm@${{ steps.ref.outputs.sha }}"
          # Wiki git repositories use master as the default branch.
          git push origin HEAD:master

content.text:
Wiki being **enabled** is only half of it. The clone failed because GitHub returns **“Repository not found”** when the token **cannot write to the wiki git repo** — not necessarily because Wiki is off.

Two common causes:

### 1. No wiki pages yet
The git repo `agent-plm.wiki.git` is created when the **first wiki page** exists. Until then, clone fails even with Wiki enabled.

**Quick fix:** open the **Wiki** tab → create any page (e.g. “Home”) → re-run the workflow.

### 2. `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write (especially after CI)
When **Publish Wiki** runs via **`workflow_run`** (after CI on `main`), GitHub gives a **read-only** token. Clone/push then fails with the same “not found” message.

**Reliable fix:** add a repository secret:

1. Create a [classic PAT](https://github.com/settings/tokens) with **`repo`** scope  
2. Repo → **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**  
3. New secret: **`WIKI_PAT`** = your token  
4. Re-run **Publish Wiki** (manual `workflow_dispatch` is fine)

Also check **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions** is **Read and write permissions** (org repos often default to read-only).

- Print wiki API diagnostics before clone

- Push to wiki branch **`master`** (wiki git default)
